conviction_note: Q3 revenue lands inside a company guide ($8-12m) that consensus already sits on, the FAA A250 market-survey authorization (Oct 21) was traded the day it came out, and the name sold its last beat-and-raise (-3.3% on 2026-08-12), so the scaled number is a near-coin-flip p_up 51 on a 7% expected absolute move; the findings sum (+0.7) is small and positive mainly because the possible upside catalysts (EXIM definitive docs, a squeeze on 8 days to cover) are asymmetric to a cash-rich balance sheet, offset by the risk of a fourth widening of the adj. EBITDA guide. The two numbers agree in sign and are both small; neither is fitted to the other.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue is pre-guided at $8-12m (adj. EBITDA $(115)-(125)m) and consensus sits at the midpoint ($10.0m EW, $10.5m Benzinga); H1 revenue was $24.8m, so a ~$10m Q3 leaves only ~$7m needed in Q4 for the $42m FY low end, while Earnings Whispers says FY consensus (~$38.9m) is still below the bottom of the raised FY range, i.e. some estimates are stale low; Q2 printed $14.7m against a prior guide reportedly $8-11m, so the company has beaten its own quarterly range before.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-12): revenue $14.7m beat consensus ~$8.5m and the FY guide was raised; stock -3.29% close-to-close. Q1 2026 (2026-05-12) -2.58%. FY25 Q4 (2026-03-09) +11.94% by the baseline window. Revenue beats have not been paid.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the quarter is inside a guide the market was given and consensus sits on its midpoint. The only unpriced piece is that stale FY estimates below the guide floor must mechanically rise; if that were priced, FY consensus would already sit at or above $42m.
findings.independence: Q3 guide confirmed separately by Quartr's Q2 call summary https://quartr.com/events/beta-technologies-inc-beta-q2-2026_F4fbeOpz; FY raise in the company's own 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001784570/000162828026055933/a2026q2earningsrelease.htm

findings.finding: On 2026-10-21 the FAA issued BETA the first special airworthiness (market survey) certificate letting its ALIA A250 eVTOL fly prospective customers, explicitly not type certification or commercial operations; a company spokesperson put component certification in 2027 and full eVTOL certification in 2028. The call is the first chance to quantify customer-demo demand and to reaffirm or move that timeline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The announcement day the stock rose 6.1% (2026-10-21), then gave it back: $19.87 on Oct 26, 1M -6.8% by Nov 2. Certification-timeline commentary has driven the name more than revenue; the May 2026 target cuts (BTIG $40->$33, Citi $33->$25) cited revised delivery expectations.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorization itself is priced (traded +6.1% and faded). What is not priced is any 2028 timeline change on the call; if the market expected a slip, the 25d skew would be wider than +6.6 and the put/call OI would not be 0.40.
findings.independence: Timeline quote from Seven Days https://www.sevendaysvt.com/?p=221974 and scope from Aviation Week https://aviationweek.com/business-aviation/safety-ops-regulation/beta-details-vtol-progress-following-faa-market-survey (different outlets, same announcement).

findings.finding: EXIM and BETA announced on 2026-08-04 an intent to expand financing to up to $1bn, about $830m incremental non-dilutive debt in tranches for manufacturing expansion (roughly doubling facility throughput), explicitly not a commitment until definitive agreements are signed; no definitive agreement or 8-K has been filed since (EDGAR filings Aug-Oct are only Forms 4/144 and 13G/A), so a signed deal or a timing update could arrive with the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No earnings-day precedent; the Aug 4 intent announcement preceded the Q2 print by eight days, and the Q2 print still fell 3.29%.
findings.why_not_priced: The intent is public; the closing is not. Earnings Whispers names cash burn as the main swing factor and asks for drawdown timing, which says the market is not treating the $830m as certain. If closing were priced, the cash-burn worry would not dominate previews. Financing question answered: the money buys manufacturing capacity for a $1.48bn-cash company with a 2028 certification path, not a rescue, so it is a positive or a zero, not a negative.
findings.independence: EDGAR submissions show no 8-K since 2026-08-12 (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001784570.json); Earnings Whispers preview flags the EXIM timing as a watch item https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/BETA/21461

findings.finding: The adj. EBITDA guide has been widened three times (now $(400)-(445)m) and Q3 is guided $(115)-(125)m with FY capex $150-200m; with H1 adj. EBITDA (Q2 alone $(109.8)m) the Q4 implied loss is large, and a fourth widening or a capex raise is the main downside path on the call, against $1.48bn cash at 2026-06-30.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Each of the last two prints carried a widened loss guide and fell (-2.58%, -3.29%); MarketBeat titled 2026-03-10 'stock price down 4.9% on disappointing earnings' while the baseline window shows +11.94% for that print.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the pattern of widening is visible and the stock is -44% from its high with sentiment at 16.8% bullish. Sized small and further shrunk for 8 days to cover short interest (a crowded short against a negative).
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers 'widened three times' https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/BETA/21461; capex range from Quartr https://quartr.com/events/beta-technologies-inc-beta-q2-2026_F4fbeOpz

findings.finding: CEO Kyle Clark has sold about $16.4M of stock in open-market sales over 21 filings in the last 12 months, at least partly under a 10b5-1 plan, with Form 144 notices filed almost every trading day from 2026-09-24 to 2026-10-30; a director (Michael Stone) bought ~$753k, last on 2026-09-03.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print-day precedent; selling has been continuous through the last two prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the sales are pre-arranged and publicly filed daily. The residual is a steady supply overhang into and after the print that caps any squeeze.
findings.independence: massive.com insider summary https://massive.com/quote/beta (aggregates the same Form 4s, so not independent of the EDGAR record).

findings.finding: Short interest more than doubled from ~6.3M shares (3.9 days to cover, 2026-06-30) to 14.59M shares (8.0 days to cover, 2026-10-15) into the print, while option open interest is call-heavy (put/call OI 0.40) and bullish sentiment collapsed to 16.8%: a positioning setup where an in-line or better print with reaffirmed timelines and an EXIM update can force covering.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-03-09 print moved +11.94% in the baseline window, the only large reaction on record; the two smaller-short prints since were -2.6% and -3.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: The +6.59 skew says the option market pays for downside, and the short base is building, so the crowd is positioned for a disappointment; a squeeze would show as rising short interest being unwound, which has not started (5d +4.4% only).
findings.independence: June figure from https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/beta/ ; sentiment from https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/BETA/21461

baseline_tension: The +6.6 put skew and doubling short interest lean down; the evidence found is mostly in-guide and priced, with the residual asymmetry (EXIM closing, a squeeze on 8 DTC, call-heavy OI) cutting mildly against the skew, so p_up sits at 51 rather than below 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short shrinks a negative): adj. EBITDA widening finding cut from -0.7 to -0.5 given 8.0 days to cover.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): EXIM finding kept positive at +0.5 after asking what the money buys (manufacturing capacity for a cash-rich company), not resized.
Lesson 1 (beats sold): Q3 revenue finding left at +0.2 and p_up moved from 50 to 51 only, because the last beat-and-raise fell 3.3%.

Note on pre_lessons order: sizes_pct are listed in draft order [revenue, FAA, EXIM, EBITDA, insider, short interest]; the draft EBITDA was -0.7 and short interest +0.5, so the draft sum was 0.2+0.3+0.5-0.7-0.3+0.5 = 0.5; the array above mis-orders two entries and should read [0.2, 0.3, 0.5, -0.7, -0.3, 0.5].
